subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What should the first browser-login handoff surface expose in Control UI: core-owned browser page, browser plugin tab using the new descriptor path, or a smaller status/resume contract first?
rationale: The source shows browser control primitives and generic plugin-tab plumbing, but the issue asks for UX, authorization, sensitive browser-state exposure, and resume semantics that require maintainer product/security boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Scope Core Handoff First
options.body: Define a minimal built-in Control UI browser handoff page for LOGIN_REQUIRED/manual-action state, profile/tab targeting, and resume against the same managed browser state.

options.title: Wait For Plugin UI Direction
options.body: Keep this blocked behind the generic plugin UI entry-point/design work and require the browser plugin to own the visible tab once that contract is accepted.

options.title: Status-Only First
options.body: Ship only browser doctor/status and exact-open links first, leaving live pixels and write controls for a later security review.

recommendation.title: Scope Core Handoff First
recommendation.body: Define a minimal built-in Control UI browser handoff page for LOGIN_REQUIRED/manual-action state, profile/tab targeting, and resume against the same managed browser state.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin-tab code ownership and the issue comment make this the best available owner for the handoff/product boundary decision.
